tier_reason: Tier C stands, but the enricher's code reading invalidates the headline fused ycrcbWithSeg row (7.4-7.6x): its channel order is mixed (the Y row treats channel 0 as B, the Cr row treats channel 0 as R, and the Cb row computes 0.564*(ch0 - Y_rgb), which is Cb in neither order), so a skin pixel BGR(120,150,220) yields (168,107,112) against OpenCV BGR2YCrCb's (168,165,101); the timed example also calls COLOR_RGB2YCrCb on BGR data, so the compared mask is not OpenCV-equivalent. The remaining CPU rows (inRange 3.5-4.0x, weightedGrayWithSeg 3.39-4.33x, grayBRWithSeg 4.6-4.8x) stand as first-party numbers with no CPU model. Correction to verifier caveat 5: weightedGray, both grayBR functions and the 1-channel inRange do use 256-bit AVX2.

corrections.claimed_speedup: CPU, same machine (1024x1280, CPU not stated): inRange 0.29-0.30 vs OpenCV 1.06-1.18 ms (3.5-4.0x); weightedGrayWithSeg 3.39-4.33x; grayBRWithSeg 4.6-4.8x. The fused ycrcbWithSeg row (0.88-0.90 ms vs cvtColor(RGB2YCrCb)+inRange 6.68-6.75 ms, 7.4-7.6x) computes a different, wrong YCrCb (mixed channel order) and should not be cited. GPU vs CPU, a different machine class (480x640, GTX 1070 kernel time vs OpenCV on an i5 7500): RGB2GRAY 0.008-0.010 vs 0.340-0.360 ms (the README cell says '3.4 - 45'; timings imply 34-45x, derived from page data). The README's RGB2HSV row compares different work and should not be cited.
